note: Document catalogue for the generator (REQ-005 FR-1): one entry per document type in document-sets.json, plus the Practice Standards self-assessment and two proposed additions. Titles, purposes, outlines and briefs are written by Readyline for the product owner's review; NOT NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission text. Standards ids and evidence aliases point at data/standards.json, which holds the Commission's wording. PO batch 7 decisions applied 12 Oct 2026: money-and-property procedure accepted into core; support planning and transitions split out; restrictive practice use register added. Batch 12 (D-041, R-7): purpose briefs are two short sentences; step-style briefs refer timeframes to fixed text; the behaviour-support steps are three sub-sections of at most eight steps. Batch 13 (D-042, R-8): review cycles (policy 12 months, register 3 months by default) are provider facts; briefs of the sections that state cycles carry the marker [review cycles] that the context pack fills in.
author: readyline

sectionModes.fixed: Rendered from template text only; the model never sees or writes it.
sectionModes.tailored: Drafted by the model from the context pack for that section, validated against the section schema, then rendered. Falls back to the template text with a 'review and complete' marker after two failed validations (FR-2).

self-assessment.heading: Standards and how we meet them

items.title: Governance policy
items.purpose: Sets out how the business is governed: who decides what, how conflicts of interest are handled, how the provider meets its registration conditions and how performance and risk are overseen.

extraSections.heading: Our structure and delegations
extraSections.brief: Describes the legal structure from the questionnaire (sole trader through to company), key personnel and who holds each delegation.

items.title: Risk management policy and register
items.purpose: Explains how risks to participants, workers and the business are identified, rated, treated and reviewed, and provides the register that records them.

extraSections.heading: Risk areas we manage
extraSections.brief: The risk areas the standard lists, each with a sentence on how it shows up for the supports delivered.

extraSections.heading: Risk register
extraSections.brief: Blank register table: risk, rating, treatment, owner, review date; sample rows marked as examples.

items.title: Continuity of supports plan
items.purpose: Shows how supports keep going when a worker is unavailable, when the provider is unavailable, or when the business changes or closes.

extraSections.heading: Cover for the provider's own absence
extraSections.brief: Present when the structure is sole trader or workers are fewer than three; names the arrangement type without naming people.

items.title: Conflict of interest policy
items.purpose: Explains how actual, potential and perceived conflicts of interest are identified, declared, recorded and managed so participants' choices are not steered.

extraSections.heading: Declaring a conflict
extraSections.brief: Declaration form and register table.

items.title: Privacy and information management policy
items.purpose: Explains how personal information is collected with consent, stored, used, shared and disposed of, and how participants' privacy and dignity are protected during supports.

extraSections.heading: Consent form
extraSections.brief: Consent to collect and use personal information, including audio or visual recording; placeholders only.

items.title: Records management policy
items.purpose: Sets out what records are kept, where, for how long, who can see them and how they are destroyed, including the records the Commission expects a registered provider to hold.

extraSections.heading: Retention schedule
extraSections.brief: Table of record type and retention period, adjusted to the supports and states; cites the source for each period or marks it for the provider to confirm.

items.title: Complaints management policy, procedure and register
items.purpose: Explains how feedback and complaints are welcomed, acknowledged, resolved, recorded and used to improve, in line with the Commission's complaints rules, and provides the register.

extraSections.heading: Complaints procedure
extraSections.brief: Numbered steps with timeframes as a table; how a participant can complain to the Commission. Never restate statutory timeframes, reportable-incident lists or the Commission's definitions; refer to the fixed section that holds them (by its number and title in the outline).

extraSections.heading: Complaints register
extraSections.brief: Register columns: reference code, date, summary, actions, outcome, improvement; warning not to record participant health details.

items.title: Incident management policy, procedure and register
items.purpose: Explains how incidents are prevented, responded to, recorded, investigated and reported, including reportable incidents to the Commission within the required timeframes, and provides the register.

extraSections.heading: Reportable incidents
extraSections.brief: The reportable incident categories and notification timeframes with the Commission source cited; no paraphrase.

extraSections.heading: Incident procedure
extraSections.brief: Numbered steps sized to the business. Never restate statutory timeframes, reportable-incident lists or the Commission's definitions; refer to the fixed section that holds them (by its number and title in the outline).

extraSections.heading: Incident register
extraSections.brief: Register columns with reference codes; participant privacy warning.

items.title: Worker screening and recruitment procedure
items.purpose: Sets out how workers and key personnel are recruited, checked and cleared, including NDIS worker screening for risk-assessed roles and the register of clearances and expiry dates.

extraSections.heading: Our risk-assessed roles
extraSections.brief: Lists the roles from the workforce answers and whether each is risk-assessed; sole-trader wording when there are no workers.

extraSections.heading: Worker screening clearance register
extraSections.brief: Columns: role, clearance type, number, expiry, next check.

items.title: Induction and training procedure and register
items.purpose: Explains how workers are inducted, trained, supervised and kept current, and provides the training register.

extraSections.heading: Training we require
extraSections.brief: Table of training by role, including anything the chosen modules require (high intensity skills, behaviour support, infection control).

extraSections.heading: Training register
extraSections.brief: Register columns.

items.title: NDIS Code of Conduct acknowledgement
items.purpose: Records that each worker and key person has read the NDIS Code of Conduct and understands what it means in this business.

items.title: Service agreement template
items.purpose: A plain-language service agreement the provider completes with each participant, covering the supports, costs, how to raise concerns, and what happens in an emergency.

extraSections.heading: Easy-read summary
extraSections.brief: One-page summary of the agreement in short sentences, prefilled with the provider's supports; participant placeholders only.

items.title: Participant rights, choice and control policy
items.purpose: Commits the provider to person-centred supports, respect for each participant's values and beliefs, and support for informed choice and dignity of risk.

extraSections.heading: How we communicate and record preferences
extraSections.brief: Describes how communication needs and support networks are recorded in support plans, by reference code only.

items.title: Safeguarding policy
items.purpose: Explains how the provider prevents, recognises and responds to violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation and discrimination, and how workers and participants can raise concerns safely.

extraSections.heading: Responding to an allegation
extraSections.brief: Steps that link to the incident procedure and the reportable incident timeframes.

items.title: Emergency and disaster management plan
items.purpose: Prepares the provider to keep participants safe and supports going through emergencies and disasters, including how supports change and how everyone is kept informed.

items.title: AI use and governance policy
items.purpose: Sets out which digital and AI tools the provider allows, for what, with what safeguards, and how human review and participant consent apply, consistent with the Commission's published position on AI.

extraSections.heading: Approved tools and uses
extraSections.brief: Table of tool category, allowed use, not allowed, and who approves; seeded from the 'existing systems' answers.

extraSections.heading: Participant information and AI
extraSections.brief: Rule: no participant personal, health or disability information goes into an AI tool unless de-identified and consented; cites the Commission position statement.

items.title: AI and digital data handling procedure
items.purpose: Step-by-step rules for de-identifying information before any AI or digital tool, recording consent, reviewing outputs and reporting mistakes.

extraSections.heading: De-identification checklist
extraSections.brief: Checklist of identifiers to remove and the reference-code convention.

items.title: Quality management and continuous improvement policy
items.purpose: Explains how the provider checks its own quality, acts on feedback, complaints, incidents and audit findings, and keeps a record of improvements.

extraSections.heading: Continuous improvement register
extraSections.brief: Columns: source, improvement, owner, due, done.

items.title: Feedback and participant engagement procedure
items.purpose: Explains how participants are asked for feedback, how it is recorded and acted on, and how supports are provided responsively, in the least intrusive way and with other providers where needed.

items.title: Support planning and transitions procedure
items.purpose: Explains how each participant's support plan is developed with them, including risk assessment and review, and how transitions into or out of the provider, including temporary ones such as hospital stays, are planned and handled.

extraSections.heading: Support plan template
extraSections.brief: Template with risk assessment, preventative health, emergency responses and annual review date; placeholders only, no participant details.

extraSections.heading: Transition checklist
extraSections.brief: Checklist for planned and unplanned transitions, including handover of records with consent.

items.title: Medication management procedure
items.purpose: Sets out how workers support participants with medication safely, including records, storage, errors and training.

items.title: Mealtime management procedure
items.purpose: Sets out how mealtime needs, including texture-modified food and fluids, are assessed, planned, delivered and reviewed safely.

items.title: Safe environment, infection control and waste procedure
items.purpose: Explains how support environments are kept safe, how workers identify themselves, how infection is prevented and how waste, including infectious and hazardous waste, is handled.

extraSections.heading: The settings we work in
extraSections.brief: Home, community, centre or vehicle, from the supports answers, each with the main hazards.

items.title: Transport safety procedure
items.purpose: Sets out vehicle, driver and participant safety rules for transport supports.

items.title: High intensity supports policy and training register
items.purpose: Commits the provider to delivering high intensity daily personal activities only through workers trained and assessed against the Commission's skills descriptors, and records that training.

extraSections.heading: High intensity supports we deliver
extraSections.brief: Which of the eight activities apply, from the supports answers; the rest are marked not delivered.

extraSections.heading: High intensity training and competency register
extraSections.brief: Columns per activity: worker role, training, assessor, date, review.

items.title: Clinical oversight procedure
items.purpose: Explains how health practitioner input, support plans and worker competence are arranged and reviewed for each high intensity support.

items.title: Restrictive practice authorisation and reporting procedure
items.purpose: Sets out how regulated restrictive practices are authorised under the relevant state or territory process, used only as described in a behaviour support plan, recorded, reported to the Commission and reduced over time.

extraSections.heading: Authorisation in the states where we work
extraSections.brief: One paragraph per state from the questionnaire, naming the authorisation body and marking anything not confirmed from a primary source.

extraSections.heading: Restrictive practice use register
extraSections.brief: Columns supporting monthly reporting; reference codes only.

items.title: Behaviour support plan implementation procedure
items.purpose: Explains how behaviour support plans, including interim plans, are obtained, understood by workers, put into practice, monitored and reviewed with the practitioner.

extraSections.heading: Steps: getting and understanding the plan
extraSections.brief: At most eight numbered steps: asking for a behaviour support plan or an interim plan, checking it is current and authorised where required, and making sure every worker who supports the participant has read and understood it. Never restate statutory timeframes, reportable-incident lists or the Commission's definitions; refer to the fixed section that holds them (by its number and title in the outline).

extraSections.heading: Steps: putting the plan into practice
extraSections.brief: At most eight numbered steps: using only the strategies in the plan, training and supervising workers on them, recording each use of a regulated restrictive practice, and what workers do when the plan does not cover a situation. Never restate statutory timeframes, reportable-incident lists or the Commission's definitions; refer to the fixed section that holds them (by its number and title in the outline).

extraSections.heading: Steps: monitoring, reporting and review
extraSections.brief: At most eight numbered steps: monthly reporting of regulated restrictive practice use, telling the practitioner what is working and what is not, reportable incidents, and asking for a plan review when needs change or the plan expires. Never restate statutory timeframes, reportable-incident lists or the Commission's definitions; refer to the fixed section that holds them (by its number and title in the outline).

extraSections.heading: Our role: practitioner or implementing provider
extraSections.brief: States which of the two modules applies from the result and adjusts the steps accordingly.

items.title: Family-centred early childhood practice procedure
items.purpose: Explains how early childhood supports are delivered with families, in natural settings, collaboratively, using evidence and measured by outcomes.

items.title: Child safe practices policy
items.purpose: Commits the provider to the rights and safety of each child, including mandatory reporting under the law of each state where it works.

extraSections.heading: Mandatory reporting where we work
extraSections.brief: One paragraph per state from the questionnaire naming the reporting scheme, marked unverified where not confirmed from a primary source.

items.title: Conflict of interest in support coordination procedure
items.purpose: Explains how conflicts between coordinating a participant's supports and delivering them are avoided, declared and managed, and how a participant's supports are managed in their interest.

items.title: Complex support escalation procedure
items.purpose: Sets out how high-risk and complex situations are recognised, escalated, coordinated with other services and reviewed.

items.title: SDA dwelling enrolment and maintenance procedure
items.purpose: Explains how dwellings are enrolled and kept compliant with the SDA rules, and how residents' rights and responsibilities are upheld.

items.title: SDA tenancy, agreements and dispute procedure
items.purpose: Explains tenancy management, the service and tenancy agreement, conflict of interest between housing and supports, and how disputes are handled.

extraSections.heading: SDA service and tenancy agreement template
extraSections.brief: Template placeholders; marked for legal review.

items.title: Supported decision-making procedure
items.purpose: Explains how participants in supported independent living are supported to make their own decisions, including about their home and daily life.

items.title: SIL safeguarding and roster oversight procedure
items.purpose: Explains dignity of risk, worker responsibilities in the home, oversight of rosters and sleepovers, and how conflict or bullying between co-tenants is prevented and handled.

items.title: SIL practice governance framework
items.purpose: Sets the vision and values for each home, how worker practice is developed and supervised, how co-tenants are matched and how emergencies in the home are overseen.

items.title: SIL tenancy, housing and support agreements procedure
items.purpose: Explains how separate agreements for supports and for tenancy or housing are made, explained and reviewed with each participant.

extraSections.heading: Agreement templates
extraSections.brief: Separate SIL service agreement and tenancy agreement templates; placeholders; marked for legal review.

items.title: Practice Standards self-assessment
items.purpose: One row per applicable standard with the Commission's outcome and indicators, how the provider meets them, the evidence to retain and a status column the provider completes before the audit.

items.title: Participant money and property procedure
items.purpose: Sets out how workers handle a participant's money or property only when asked, with records and safeguards.
